outline: Biostatistics, Epidemiology/Population Health, & Interpretation of the Medical Literature
diagnosis: Correct interpretation of a noninferiority trial confidence interval
mechanism: In a noninferiority trial, the confidence interval for the prespecified treatment-effect contrast is compared with a clinically justified noninferiority margin. If the entire confidence interval excludes the region worse than the margin, noninferiority is demonstrated. Superiority generally requires the confidence interval also to exclude the null value in the favorable direction.
vignette: A randomized trial compares a new oral therapy with an established active treatment. The primary outcome is treatment success. Before enrollment, investigators prespecify a noninferiority margin of -5 percentage points for the difference in success rates (new therapy minus standard therapy). The observed difference is -1.2 percentage points, with a 95% confidence interval of -3.4 to +1.0 percentage points.
lead: Which of the following is the most appropriate interpretation of these results?
correct: The new therapy meets the prespecified criterion for noninferiority but has not demonstrated superiority to the standard therapy
distractors: The new therapy is inferior because the point estimate favors the standard therapy
The new therapy is superior because part of the confidence interval lies above zero
Noninferiority has not been demonstrated because the confidence interval includes zero
The therapies have been proven equivalent because the confidence interval lies within 5 percentage points of zero
distractor_notes: A point estimate slightly favoring the control does not establish inferiority when the entire confidence interval remains above the prespecified -5-point noninferiority boundary.
Superiority would require the confidence interval to exclude the null value in the favorable direction; this interval includes zero.
Including zero prevents a superiority conclusion but does not prevent noninferiority when the entire interval remains on the acceptable side of the noninferiority margin.
A successful noninferiority test is not the same as proving exact equivalence. Equivalence requires a prespecified two-sided equivalence framework and margins.
key_expl: The entire 95% confidence interval (-3.4 to +1.0) is above the prespecified noninferiority margin of -5 percentage points, so outcomes worse than the standard by 5 points or more are excluded and noninferiority is demonstrated. Because the interval crosses 0, a superiority claim is not supported. Noninferiority does not by itself prove equivalence.
objective: Interpret a noninferiority trial by comparing the full confidence interval with the prespecified noninferiority margin and separately evaluating whether superiority is supported.
clues: CI above margin but crosses zero
